The Night Market: 游客逛夜市的见闻与感受。
When I visited Taiwan last summer, the most exciting place was the night market. As soon as the sun went down, hundreds of small shops opened along both sides of the street.

The smells were amazing. Cooks made noodles, soup and grilled meat in front of you, and the smoke rose into the warm night air. I tried a famous snack called 'small buns in soup'. They were so delicious that I ate two bowls!

The market was not only about food. There were games, clothes and toys everywhere. Children played simple games to win small gifts, and old men played chess under bright lights. I bought a pair of cheap shoes and a hat with a funny picture on it.

The best thing about the night market was the people. Shop owners smiled and joked with each other, and nobody seemed in a hurry. In my city, shops close at eight in the evening. Here, life only starts when the stars come out. I understood why locals love their night markets so much.
